description: Generates a Node.js + TypeScript command-line application with the same opinionated stack and layered structure as stackfold: commander, @inquirer/prompts, execa, cosmiconfig and zod, wired as ports and adapters, with unit tests on in-memory fakes and an integration test that runs the built binary.

help.name: Node CLI
help.details: Runtime dependencies: commander, @inquirer/prompts, execa, cosmiconfig, zod. Dev tooling: typescript, vitest, @types/node. Layout: cli/ -> core/ <- infra/, assembled in one composition root. Ships two sample commands (greet, doctor). Questions: projectName, description, binName, author.

rules.message: Project name must be a lowercase npm-style name: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,213}$

maxLength.message: Description must be 200 characters or fewer.

rules.message: Description must not contain control characters.
Description must be a single line.

questions.message: Command name (the executable users will type)?

rules.message: Command name must be lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting with a hyphen: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,213}$

maxLength.message: Author must be 150 characters or fewer.

rules.message: Author must not contain control characters.
Author must be a single line.

# {{{projectName}}}

{{{description}}}

## Requirements

- Node.js 22.18.0 or later.

## Install

Build the project and install the command globally:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm install -g .
{{{binName}}} --help
```

To try it without installing it globally, run `npm start -- greet World` after `npm run build`.

## Usage

### greet

```bash
{{{binName}}} greet [name] [--times <n>] [--shout]
```

Prints `<greeting>, <name>!`. When `name` is omitted in an interactive terminal, the command asks for it. When no terminal is attached, a missing `name` is an error.

- `--times <n>` prints the greeting `n` times. `n` must be a positive integer.
- `--shout` prints the greeting in upper case.

```bash
{{{binName}}} greet World --times 2 --shout
# HELLO, WORLD!
# HELLO, WORLD!
```

### doctor

```bash
{{{binName}}} doctor
```

Runs `node --version` and prints the result, for example `node: v22.18.0`. It fails with a non-zero exit code when `node` cannot be run.

### Errors and debugging

Errors raised by the CLI are printed to stderr as `Error: <message>` and the command exits with a non-zero code. Usage errors reported by the argument parser (for example `--times 0`) use the parser's own `error: ...` format instead. Set `DEBUG=1` to print the stack trace as well:

```bash
DEBUG=1 {{{binName}}} greet World
```

## Configuration

`greet` reads its defaults from a configuration file. The search starts in the current directory and climbs through the parent directories until it reaches the first directory that contains a `package.json`, which is the last one searched. In each directory it looks for these files, in this order:

- `.{{{binName}}}rc`
- `.{{{binName}}}rc.json`
- `{{{binName}}}.config.json`

The file holds a JSON object. Every key is optional:

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `greeting` | string | `"Hello"` | The word that starts the greeting. |
| `times` | positive integer | `1` | How many times to print the greeting. |
| `shout` | boolean | `false` | Print the greeting in upper case. |

```json
{ "greeting": "Howdy", "times": 2 }
```

A command-line flag overrides the same setting in the file. An invalid value, or a key that is not listed above, stops the command with an error that names the file and the key.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run build       # compile src/ to dist/
npm run typecheck   # type-check without emitting files
npm test            # unit tests, then the integration tests against the built binary
npm start -- greet World
```

`npm test` compiles the project before it runs the integration tests, so it works on a fresh clone.

## Project structure

```text
{{{projectName}}}/
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  vitest.config.ts
  src/
    cli/
      index.ts              composition root: creates the adapters and wires the commands
      commands/greet.ts     the greet command
      commands/doctor.ts    the doctor command
    core/
      ports.ts              interfaces: Prompter, ProcessRunner, ConfigStore
      config.ts             the configuration schema and its defaults
    infra/
      prompter.ts           Prompter over @inquirer/prompts
      processRunner.ts      ProcessRunner over execa
      configStore.ts        ConfigStore over cosmiconfig
  tests/
    unit/                   commands and core, with in-memory fakes of the ports
    integration/cli.test.ts the built binary with the real adapters
```

Dependencies point inward: `cli/` and `infra/` depend on `core/`, and `core/` imports nothing from them and no package except `zod`. Commands receive their ports as arguments, so tests replace the adapters with fakes. `tests/unit/architecture.test.ts` checks these rules.
